body:
Implements the scope proposed in discussion #611: https://github.com/qelectrotech/qelectrotech-source-mirror/discussions/611

## The gap this closes

`DiagramContext` (the free-form key/value store backing every element's info fields) already accepts and round-trips any key matching `^[a-z0-9-_]+$` generically via `toXml()`/`fromXml()`. But `ElementInfoWidget::buildInterface()` only ever builds one row per key from the fixed ~40 predefined `ELMT_*` constants — there was no way for a user to actually create a new key through the properties dialog, even though the storage layer already fully supported it.

## What this adds

- A new **"Ajouter une propriété personnalisée"** button at the bottom of the element Informations panel.
- Clicking it appends a `CustomElementInfoPartWidget` row — unlike the existing fixed `ElementInfoPartWidget` rows (each hardcoded to one predefined key), both the key name and the value are user-editable here.
- The typed key is validated live against the already-public `DiagramContext::isKeyAcceptable()` and the field gets a red border the moment it doesn't match, instead of the key silently failing to save.
- `ElementInfoWidget::updateUi()` now also scans the element's current informations for any key outside the predefined/special set and rebuilds a custom row for each — so a previously-added custom property re-displays correctly the next time that element is selected or the project is reopened.
- No changes needed to `DiagramContext::toXml()`/`fromXml()` — custom keys flow through the exact same generic path predefined keys already use.
- A remove button on each custom row deletes that property.

## Testing

Built clean, no new warnings. Verified end-to-end in a real GUI session (Xvfb) against `examples/741.qet`:
- Selected a resistor element, clicked "Ajouter une propriété personnalisée", typed key `puissance_max` / value `250W`, saved the project.
- Confirmed in the saved XML that `puissance_max` was written as a normal `<elementInformation>` entry alongside the predefined keys, with no special-casing needed.
- Fully restarted the app, reloaded the project, reselected the same element: the custom row reappeared pre-filled with `puissance_max` / `250W`.
- Edited the key to `Invalid Key!` (uppercase + space, violates the accepted key format) and confirmed the field immediately shows a red border.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

commits.messageBody:
ElementInfoWidget's fixed ~40 predefined ELMT_* keys had no way for a
user to add a genuinely new element-info key, even though DiagramContext
already stores/round-trips arbitrary keys generically via toXml()/fromXml().

Adds an "Ajouter une propriété personnalisée" button that appends a
CustomElementInfoPartWidget row (both key and value user-editable,
unlike the fixed ElementInfoPartWidget rows bound to one predefined
key). The typed key is validated live against the existing
DiagramContext::isKeyAcceptable() and flagged with a red border when
it doesn't match, instead of silently dropping it. Any key already
present on the element that isn't one of the predefined/special keys
is re-displayed as a custom row on next selection.

Implements the scope proposed in discussion #611.
